description: It’s 1984 and MIT professor Rodney Brooks has a radical idea: robots don't need complicated brains to navigate the world — they just need simple rules. Brooks and two of his students, Colin Angle and Helen Greiner, turn that idea into a company called iRobot. The company chases government contracts and builds robotic dolls. But in 2002, iRobot breaks through with the Roomba — a vacuuming robot. The Roomba bumps into chair legs, takes cats for joyrides, and propels iRobot to a blockbuster IPO. Bu…
classificationReason: A focused account of iRobot, Rodney Brooks's navigation ideas, and the development and commercialization of Roomba.
qualityReason: Likely substantive narrative analysis of a major robotics company's technology and business trajectory.
